business.description: GTL Infrastructure Limited is an IP-1 registered entity engaged in providing passive telecom infrastructure on a shared basis to mobile telecommunications service providers for hosting active network equipment. The Company's business model is built around the ownership, operation and maintenance of passive telecom infrastructure supporting multiple technologies, with infrastructure sharing and energy management constituting its key service offerings.

outlook.statement: India's telecom infrastructure sector is expected to benefit from continued network densification, rural coverage expansion and technology upgrades, supported by ongoing 4G/5G roll-outs, rising broadband adoption and BharatNet expansion. Industry forecasts indicate tenancy growth of about 5–6% for tower companies in the current and ensuing financial year.

The Company remains focused on increasing tower utilisation through incremental tenancies and loadings, strengthening customer relationships, improving operational and energy efficiency, protecting the asset base and maintaining high network availability. Disciplined capital allocation, counterparty risk management and continued progress on debt restructuring/settlement will remain important to strengthening the Company's financial resilience.

The Company is at an advanced stage of discussions with its remaining Rupee Term Loan lenders under the settlement framework agreed at the Joint Lenders' Meeting. Building on the progress achieved during the year, the Company remains focused on completing the resolution of the remaining debt through mutually agreed bilateral settlements and establishing a sustainable capital structure to support its operations and long-term business objectives.

Company believes combination of sectorial recovery, lenders settlement, proactive protection measures and sustained customer engagement will support gradual stabilisation of operations, reduction of legacy risks associated with unoccupied sites and long-term revival of the business.

Telecom sector is witnessing positive developments supported by policy and regulatory measures, continued network expansion, increasing data consumption and investments in 4G/5G, fibreisation and digital connectivity, which are expected to create long-term opportunities for telecom infrastructure providers.
HR priorities for FY 2026-27 centre on deepening gains in leadership diversity, digital capability, and employee-centric policy while keeping safety and compliance non-negotiable.
During FY 2026-27 the Company aims to further electrify 7 no. of sites

Expansion to support new technologies, including 5G, requires significant annual CAPEX allocation to address growing customer future requirements. Sites are undergoing upgrades of SMPS and Battery Banks under the CAPEX material in coming years.
Company has forecasted a stable movement of tenancies in future years, attributed to the resolution of disputes with its customers, forming a key basis for going concern assessment.
Strategic focus on EBITDA optimization and revenue enhancement through anticipation of additional tenancies on telecom towers.
The management believes that the ongoing positive momentum in the telecom sector will lead to increased demand for the Company's tower infrastructure, thereby supporting growth in revenue and EBITDA.

Positive developments expected to support long-term growth and stabilisation: lenders' settlement and debt resolution progress, favourable telecom sector developments (government policy support, VIL capital strengthening, Airtel/Jio 5G rollouts, BSNL revival, subscriber growth, ARPU improvements), internal resource optimization, lock-in period extensions, and pursuit of contractual claims of approx. ₹15,01,135 Lakhs from customers for premature exits. Company has no intention to discontinue operations and continues as Going Concern.

The telecom sector is also witnessing positive developments supported by policy and regulatory measures, continued network expansion, increasing data consumption and investments in 4G / 5G, fibreisation and digital connectivity, which are expected to create long-term opportunities for telecom infrastructure providers.

Telecom sector and market risk: Revenue dependent on stability and growth of Indian telecom sector, influenced by spectrum costs, regulatory developments, technology cycles, competitive intensity, customer network strategies and financial position of telecom operators

Operator consolidation, competition and tenancy risk: Market concentrated with ~4 key operators (Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel, VIL, BSNL) accounting for ~92.7% of wireless subscribers; operators continue to optimize networks and may exit/relocate/consolidate sites; competition from aligned infrastructure providers (Summit Digital for Jio, Indus Towers for Airtel) may limit new tenancy allocation

Credit and customer concentration risk: Exposure to counterparty credit risk, delayed collections, disputed deductions and customer concentration; financial and liquidity conditions vary significantly among operators

Liquidity and debt resolution risk: Principal sources of liquidity are operating cash flows, customer collections, contractual deposits, cost optimisation and property monetisation; sensitive to tenancy levels, payment cycles, energy/rental costs, statutory demands and timing of lender settlements

Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds risk: Trustee of Series A FCCB filed Commercial Suit for recovery of US$ 27 Mn; Series B2 Bonds matured October 27, 2022 with conversion rights exercisable; 36% of outstanding bonds converted to equity since maturity

Property tax and municipal levy risk: Local authorities raising demands on telecom towers; Section 14 of Telecommunications Act 2023 provides exemption but certain authorities continue to raise demands

Customer recovery and legacy recovery risk: Substantial claims against former operators (Aircel Group, RCom/Reliance Telecom/SSTL, Videocon) undergoing insolvency; recovery uncertain due to priority of secured creditors, limited asset base, Supreme Court ruling on spectrum treatment

Arbitration and judicial proceedings risk: Prolonged arbitration with vendor settled and withdrawn; DRT proceedings pending with Rupee Term Loan lenders; adverse outcome could affect liquidity and financial position

The Company continues to carry accumulated losses from earlier years and had also incurred a loss before exceptional items during the financial year 2025-26. Accordingly, the availability of adequate profits in each financial year during the proposed tenure of Mr. Jayant Bhimanwar cannot be assured.

The Company has lost approximately 69,743 tenancies as a result of shutting down of major telecom operators. Consequently, more than 14,000 towers sites, abandoned by discontinuing operators became unoccupied (which was more than 50% of the total tower portfolio). These discontinuing operators did not make any payment of their contractual dues to the Company, including rent payable to landlords, statutory dues such as property tax, NA tax, local body tax, employees' dues and vendors' claims etc., many of which are pass through payments for the Company. As a result, the Company was saddled with substantial costs and liabilities including rents, vendors' claims and statutory dues on such unoccupied towers without any revenue.

Increase in productivity and EBITDA levels depends upon the developments in the telecom industry, recovery of the Company's contractual claims, availability of cash flows and completion of remaining debt resolution.
